notes.2: Most candidates were able to correctly reject option D , but all other options were popular responses. Candidates should recall that a substance will be a liquid at a temperature between the melting and boiling points.
notes.4: All the options were chosen in a ratio that suggests many were guessing the position of the solvent front.
notes.8: Options A and B were the most common incorrect answers selected. In option A , candidates assumed that the number of hydrogen atoms was equal to the number of bonding electrons and for option B , candidates counted the correct number of bonds but did not recall that each bond would contain two electrons.
notes.12: Although most candidates gave the correct option, C , option B was also chosen frequently suggesting that many candidates were unclear which particle was chosen as the comparison for relative masses.
notes.13: The majority of candidates incorrectly chose option A or option B . The question tells candidates that the initial solution was neutral so the initial colour should be green not blue.
notes.20: Most candidates identified the correct colour change but thought that the addition of water would cause the temperature to fall.
notes.21: Properties of acids and bases were not commonly known. Although option A , the correct answer, was the most common option chosen, the distribution of options chosen suggested many candidates were guessing.
notes.29: Option C was a popular incorrect choice. The majority of candidates incorrectly chose a solid ionic substance as an electrical conductor, not recognising that the alloy would be a solid conductor.
notes.36: Option C , the key, was the least popular answer. Candidates did not recognise that three fractions had been chosen and the boiling point was not listed in descending order.
notes.38: Most candidates thought that yeast is fermented rather than glucose. Only a minority were able to identify water as steam as a product of combustion of ethanol.
notes.40: Most candidates were able to recall the reaction of acids with CaCO 3 and their effect on methyl red but did not recognise CuO as a basic oxide, which would also react. The incorrect option D was the most popular answer.
notes.general_comments: Questions 3 , 7 , 10 , 15 , 17 , 19 and 32 had the lowest demand. Questions 8 , 20 , 29 , 36 , 38 and 40 were found to be more challenging. Overall the questions on organic chemistry were least well answered.
